documents.title: Doc 51 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - off track and gained lasting advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - off track and gained lasting advantage

details.fact: Car 6 (Tsolov) went off track while passing Car 9 (Mini) and gained lasting advantage.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Five seconds (5) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (a) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 48 & 49) and heard the Drivers of Car 6 (Tsolov) and Car 9 (Mini) and the team representatives. The Stewards, together with the Drivers and Team Representatives, reviewed video evidence including CCTV and drone footage, TV host high resolution images and Cars’ 6, 9, and 15 onboard cameras. The Driver of Car 6 explained that he was on soft tyres and he attacked Car 9 at the breaking point of Turn 10, where Car 9 ran wide. Due to the different tyre strategy, it was a simple move at the exit of Turn 10 and entry of Turn 11. He stated that he did not leave the track and that the move was already completed. The Driver Car 9 explained that he was defending the position, and that he exited turn 10 quite tight leaving a lot of room at the inside of Turn 11 for Car 6. He also stated that Car 6 left the track and gained a lasting advantage by completing the manoeuvre off track. Having considered that matter extensively the Stewards determined that Car 6 left the track at Turn 11 and completed an overtaking move by exceeding the track limits. The Stewards find that mitigating circumstances exist to impose a 5 second time penalty on this occasion rather than the usual penalty of 10 seconds. The mitigating circumstances are that Car 6 left the track at Turn 11 for a extremely short period of time, video evidence also confirmed that despite Car 6 being off track, the distance to the white line was marginal, to the extent that the Stewards’ needed the TV host high resolution images to determine that an infringement was committed.

documents.title: Doc 39 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 22 - left the track and gained lasting advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 22 - left the track and gained lasting advantage

details.fact: Car 22 (Varrone) left the track at Turn 1 and gained lasting advantage over Car 11 (Montoya).
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Five seconds (5) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (a) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 31 & 32) and heard the Drivers of Car 22 (Varrone) and Car 11 (Montoya) and the team representatives. They examined video evidence and onboard footage. During the hearing the Driver of Car 11 stated that he was ahead at the apex and he had the right of the corner. He also stated that at the apex, Car 22 moved slightly to the right, forcing him slightly to the kerb, which caused his car to snap, and contact with Car 22. That circumstance was confirmed by his team representative who added that the cars were alongside at the apex and it was not a dive in manoeuvre. The Driver of Car 22 stated that he was defending the position and he received a small contact due to a snap from Car 11 and, for that reason, Car 22 had to go off track and followed the escape road. The team representative of Car 22 also stated that his driver in this position could not have disappeared and it was the reason why he had to leave the track. The Stewards determined that the Drivers of Car 22 and Car 11 were fighting for position at Turn 1. Car 11 made an attempt to overtake and at the apex of Turn 1 was ahead of Car 22 that was defending the position. During the manoeuvre, Car 11 had a slight touch with Car 22 who at that moment lost the right of the turn. For the contact the Stewards found that no drivers were wholly or predominately to blame. However after the small contact, Car 22 went out of the track by using the escape road and in doing so gained the position on Car 11 when he rejoined the track. On this occasion, the Stewards consider that if a car defending the position leaves the track and re-joins in the same position, it has to be considered as having gained a lasting advantage. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards noted that in this specific case despite Car 22 trying to give some of the advantage back, the driver was unable to do it fully as Car 14 had overtaken Car 11. Therefore, the Stewards elected to assess a lower penalty than the baseline for such an offence.

documents.title: Doc 33 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 14 - contact to Car 2 in Race 1
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 14 - contact to Car 2 in Race 1

details.fact: Car 14 (Stenshorne) made contact with Car 2 (Durksen) at Turn 12 in Race 1 (Sprint Race).
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 2 points.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. Car 14 (Stenshorne) attempted an overtake on the outside of Car 2 (Dürksen) on Turn 10 into Turn 11. Car 2 edged ahead of Car 14. As they entered Turn 12, Car 14 did not manage to establish sufficient overlap to be given racing room. Car 14 kept his line on the inside, and collided with Car 2, causing it to go off-track. The Stewards determine that Car 14 was wholly responsible for the collision and elect to apply the standard penalty.

documents.title: Doc 24 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 2 - failed to respect yellow flags in Qualifying
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 2 - failed to respect yellow flags in Qualifying

details.fact: Car 2 (Durksen) failed to respect the yellow flag requirements at Turn 14 in Qualifying, where Car 3 (Miyata) had crashed.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L Chapter IV, Article 1 and Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A drop of 5 places on the grid for the Sprint Race & Feature Race at this Competition, as per Article 31.5 of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 5 points
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 19) and heard the Driver of Car 2 (Durksen) and the team representative. The FIA F2 Technical Delegate and the F2 Technical Director were also present during the hearing. The Stewards examined GPS, car data, marshalling sector times and video evidence. The Driver of Car 2 explained that as soon as he finished the corner (Turn 14), he received the yellow flag and saw Car 3 (Miyata) in the wall. He stated that he was under control of the situation, and considered it safe, as Car 3 was far away from the track. The team representative stated that there was a short time from the yellow flag until the end of the lap, therefore Car 2 did not have sufficient time to react to the flag. Video evidence shows marshal post 16.6 waving a single yellow flag while Car 2 is exiting Turn 14. The marshalling sector chart showed that in mini sector 16, which covered the single yellow flag area, the driver set his fastest sector time of the session. Having considered the matter extensively, Stewards determined that Car 2 failed to reduce the speed under a single yellow flag condition. Car data confirmed that Car 2 didn’t brake earlier and/or noticeably reduce the speed in that sector as required by Appendix H Article 2.5.5 b) of the FIA International Sporting Code. Therefore, Stewards decide to impose the standard penalty of a drop of 5 grid positions for both Sprint and Feature race plus 2 penalty points.

documents.title: Doc 21 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 3 - sole cause of the issuance of the red flag
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 3 - sole cause of the issuance of the red flag

details.fact: Car 3 (Miyata) was the sole cause of the issuance of the red flag at 16:21 in Qualifying.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 33.5 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Deletion of the fastest lap time set by Car 3 in Qualifying. A result of the fastest lap deletion, Car 3 is now outside 107% of the fastest qualifying time. Permission is given for Car 3 to start the Sprint Race and Feature Race from the back of the grid, in accordance with Article 34.2 of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 18) and heard the Driver of Car 3 (Miyata) and the team representative. They examined video evidence. The Stewards determined that Car 3 went off at Turn 14. The Race Director red flagged the session due to this incident. The driver explained that he lost control of the car while approaching the turn, resulting in a collision with the wall. The team representative stated that they were unable to review the car's data to determine whether a technical malfunction had occurred. The Stewards decided to pause the hearing for one hour, allowing the team time to review the car's data with supervision from the Technical Delegate. This break was intended to ensure the team could thoroughly investigate any potential technical issues before the proceedings continued. Following the review, the team representative confirmed that the driver approached the turn at a higher speed, attributing the incident to Miyata's error. Having considered the matter, the Stewards determined that Car 3 was the sole cause of the issuance of the red flag. The Stewards concluded that the failure of the driver to negotiate Turn 14 was within the driver and team’s control and such a penalty is warranted.

documents.title: Doc 20 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - breach of Article 22.15 (shorts in pit lane)
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - breach of Article 22.15 (shorts in pit lane)

details.fact: Member of team personnel of Campos Racing (Car 6) wearing short trousers in the Working Area of the Pit Lane.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 22.15 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: A fine of 500 Euros to be paid by the Competitor. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 17) and heard the team representative. They examined photographic and video evidence. During the hearing the team representative explained that the man wearing shorts was the physio of Car 6 and not an operational team member. Consistent with previous decisions the Stewards apply the rule to all personnel working near the car including physios. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that a member of Car 6 working near the car was not wearing long trousers during the session as required by the Sporting Regulations and therefore decided to fine the team with 500 Euros.

documents.title: Doc 15 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 8 - unsafe release in Practice
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 8 - unsafe release in Practice

details.fact: Car 8 (Bilinski) was released in the path of Car 24 (Van Hoepen) at the start of the session.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 28.12 (a) of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: A fine of 500 Euros to be paid by the Competitor. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 12) and heard the Driver of Car 8 (Bilinski) and the team representative. They examined video evidence. The Driver of Car 8 explained that he was released by his mechanic and he was just following the teams’ instructions. The Team representative admitted that the number one mechanic released Car 8 in a potentially dangerous manner. Having considered the matter extensively, Stewards determined that Car 8 was released in an unsafe manner by the team. The Stewards determined that the driver was not at fault. Consequently, following the Stewards Guidelines the team has been issued the standard fine of 500 Euros.
